basis.governing_question: How does Farmácias Lusas choose an ERP, migrate its data and roll it out to its 40 pharmacies and 2 warehouses?

sub_questions.question: What must the new ERP do for finance, purchasing and inventory in the pharmacies and warehouses?
Where do the current processes and systems fit a standard ERP, and where are the gaps?
Which ERP vendor best meets the requirements, and does the business case support selecting it?
How can data from the current finance, purchasing and inventory systems be migrated reliably into the new ERP?
Is the new ERP running for finance, purchasing and inventory in all 40 pharmacies and both warehouses?

work.unit: Process area mapped with its requirements

phase_work.why: Three process areas mapped two at a time, then one; leader interviews run alongside the mapping. Within the typical 3-6 weeks.
One shortlist, demonstration and scoring cycle, with the business case built alongside its second half. Within the typical 4-8 weeks.

work.unit: System configured and tested for one process area
Rollout wave of up to 10 sites

phase_work.why: Three areas configured two at a time, one migration rehearsal, one pilot site, then five waves for the remaining sites.

sizing.levers: Running all three process areas at once, or larger rollout waves, would shorten the engagement most; a narrower first scope would also help.

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Map finance, purchasing and inventory processes in the pharmacies and warehouses and define what the new ERP must do.

gate.label: Requirements sign-off
gate.decision: Go ahead with vendor selection on the signed-off requirements and process fit?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Score ERP vendors against the agreed requirements and build the business case for the selection decision.

gate.label: Go/no-go on selection
gate.decision: Which ERP vendor goes forward, and is the case strong enough to start implementation?

phases.name: Implementation
phases.objective_one_line: Configure the ERP, migrate data and bring it live in all 40 pharmacies and both warehouses.

gate.label: Final acceptance
gate.decision: Approve the ERP as running in all 40 pharmacies and both warehouses?

architect_notes: Length is an estimate (36-42 weeks); Implementation takes the middle of 23-34, and 3-week waves with 6-week configuration would push it to the top.
Design assumes no formal tender; one would add 4 to 6 weeks, so confirm whether Farmácias Lusas must run a tender.
No Change & Training phase: the brief does not name it; confirm whether staff training and adoption need their own phase.
Implementation added to the archetype's Diagnostic and Design phases because the brief asks for data migration and rollout to all sites.
